extracted.intended_audience: manufacturers, private labelers, trade associations, consumer advocates, legal counsel, and CPSC staff involved with CPSA section 6(b)/15(b) disclosures and FOIA
extracted.subtask_description: Analysis and proposed revisions to 16 CFR part 1101 implementing CPSA section 6(b), including when the Commission must provide notice/opportunity to comment, exceptions to nondisclosure, procedural timing, and how publicly-available or Commission-obtained information is treated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reproduction accompanying request
rubrics_metrics.description: A reproduction of the disclosure (e.g., image, audio or video file, copy of document) should accompany the request, if practicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposed update to reflect technological advancements since 1983; suggests attaching an actual copy of the disclosure when submitting a request to the Commission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filer's characterization controls application of section 6(b)(5)
rubrics_metrics.description: Absent exceptional circumstances where a filing clearly does not come within the requirements of section 15(b), the Commission will rely, for purposes of applying section 6(b)(5), upon the filer's own characterization of its filing as being submitted pursuant to section 15(b) and 16 CFR 1115.13.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even if the firm refuses to admit or specifically denies that the information reasonably supports a conclusion of noncompliance or hazard, the Commission will continue to apply 6(b)(5)'s disclosure limitations when a firm indicates it is making a submission pursuant to section 15(b) and 16 CFR 1115.13, except in exceptional cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification requirement for section 15(b) submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: A submitting firm must identify the information as submitted pursuant to both section 15(b) of the CPSA and 16 CFR 1115.13.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 16 CFR 1115.13 specifies required content for initial and full reports under section 15(b); the proposed change makes explicit that submissions intended to receive 6(b)(5) treatment must be so identified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remedial settlement agreements include corrective action plans and consent orders
rubrics_metrics.description: Corrective action plans and consent orders are examples of 'remedial settlement agreements' where section 6(b)(5)'s additional disclosure limitations do not apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Legislative history and long-standing Commission interpretation support that both formal documents (e.g., consent orders) and informal agreements (e.g., corrective action plans, letters) can qualify as remedial settlement agreements exempting disclosure protections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure upon consent
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission may disclose information submitted pursuant to section 15(b) without following the requirements of section 6(a) or 6(b) if the person who submitted the information under section 15(b) agrees to its public disclosure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This covers negotiated, consensual releases (e.g., recall alert/news release) between Commission staff and manufacturers/private labelers; section 6 notice is not required for such consensual releases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public health and safety exception (6(b)(5)(D))
rubrics_metrics.description: Paragraph (4) applies the exception where 'The Commission publishes a finding that the public health and safety requires public disclosure with a lesser period of notice than is required by section 6(b)(1).'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Legislative history suggests public health/safety findings can trigger an exception to certain 6(b) protections; the Commission solicits comment on whether sections 6(b)(2) and 6(b)(3) apply when a public health and safety finding is invoked under 6(b)(5)(D).

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure after complying with sections 6(a) and 6(b)(1)-(3)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission may disclose, in certain instances, information submitted pursuant to 15(b) of the CPSA only after complying with the requirements of sections 6(a) and 6(b)(1)-(3) of the CPSA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposed conforming text change to reflect statutory cross-references (adding 'sections 6(a) and 6(b)(1)-(3)').

rubrics_metrics.name: Publicly available information excluded from 6(b)(5)
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 6(b)(5) does not apply to information that is already available to the public, including but not limited to information appearing in a company's press statements, websites, Frequently Asked Questions, product user manuals, sales materials, Securities and Exchange Commission filings, or other public statements or documents published or publicly disseminated by a manufacturer, distributor, or retailer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: news reports; academic/scientific articles; press releases; internet-available information; SaferProducts.gov postings; retail locations or sale prices. The Commission's revised approach: it will release or identify information obtained from public sources only if (1) it does not characterize the publicly available information or relay new information, and (2) the Commission's use of the information is accurate and not misleading.

rubrics_metrics.name: Independently obtained/prepared or developed through Commission investigation
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 6(b)(5) does not apply to information independently obtained or prepared, or developed through subsequent investigation and verification, by the Commission, any member of the Commission, or any employee, agent, or representative, including contractor, of the Commission in an official capacity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A firm submitting a section 15(b) report must provide copies or a summary of complaints and, upon request, names/addresses of distributors, retailers, purchasers. The Commission may contact consumers, retailers, distributors to obtain additional information; 6(b)(5) should not preclude such investigative activity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope includes Commission-generated documents and oral communications
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 6(b)(5)'s additional disclosure limitations apply not just to documents generated by staff but also to documents generated by the Commission, any member of the Commission, or any employee, agent, or representative, including contractor, of the Commission in an official capacity, and to any oral communications made by these individuals or the Commission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposed text clarifies that both written and oral Commission-originated communications are within the regulation's scope where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing measured in calendar days
rubrics_metrics.description: Insert the word 'calendar' before 'days' throughout part 1101 where timing is specified so that notice and comment timing is calculated in calendar days.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This aligns with Commission practice since 2008 and removes ambiguity caused by mixed references to 'days' and 'calendar days.' Commenters argued business days would be less burdensome; Commission maintains calendar days are correct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Information must permit public to ascertain manufacturer/private labeler identity
rubrics_metrics.description: The manner in which the consumer product is designated or described in the information must permit the public to ascertain readily the identity of the manufacturer or private labeler (see §1101.13).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposed deletion of a prior regulatory requirement that also the product itself be identifiable; the revision adheres more closely to statutory language that focuses on ascertainment of the manufacturer's identity for 6(b)(1) notice triggers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section 6(b) exemption for rulemaking proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: The requirements of sections 6(b)(1)-(3) shall not apply to the public disclosure of 'information in the course of or concerning a rulemaking proceeding (which shall commence upon the publication of an advance notice of proposed rulemaking or a notice of proposed rulemaking).' (15 U.S.C. 2055(b)(4)(B))
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Commission will not apply 6(b) notice/opportunity-to-comment requirements to rulemaking proceedings, recognizing statutory exemption.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability to individuals acting in official capacity
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission, any member of the Commission, or any employee, agent, or representative, including contractor, of the Commission in an official capacity must propose to disclose the information to the public (see §1101.12).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarifies that section 6's provisions apply whenever the Commission or specified individuals in official capacities propose disclosure; deletion of prior verbose phrasing was proposed to avoid confusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reports of harm on SaferProducts.gov excluded from 6(b)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reports of harm posted on SaferProducts.gov are explicitly excluded from the scope of the statutory 6(b) requirements by statute and current regulations (15 U.S.C. 2055a(f)(1); 16 CFR 1102.44(a)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Once posted publicly to SaferProducts.gov, these reports are treated as public information and can be used or released without 6(b) notice, subject to accuracy and non-misleading use. Reports of harm that the Commission has not published on SaferProducts.gov remain subject to 6(b) notice requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subsequent disclosures and renotification standard
rubrics_metrics.description: The 6(b) Regulation will specify that the requirements of section 6(b)(1) do not apply to: 'Information, not previously disclosed, that in context does not disclose materially more or materially different information about the consumer product than what the Commission previously disclosed in accordance with the law.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Commission adopts an approach to avoid needing fresh notice for disclosures that do not materially change the substance of previously disclosed information; renotification is not required for firms to provide new data to the Commission, and the Commission has an ongoing duty under 6(b)(7) to ensure disclosures are accurate and not misleading.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section 15(b) report content requirements (complaints and distribution info)
rubrics_metrics.description: A firm submitting a section 15(b) report must provide copies or a summary of any complaints related to the safety of the product (16 CFR 1115.13(d)(6)). Upon request, the submitting firm must provide the names and addresses of all distributors, retailers, and purchasers, including consumers, of the product (16 CFR 1115.13(d)(14)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These content requirements enable the Commission to investigate and independently develop information; they are cited to justify Commission contacts and verification activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: FOIA-related 6(b) notice procedures and opportunities to review
rubrics_metrics.description: For FOIA requests, the 6(b)(1) notice includes a copy of the materials the Commission proposes to disclose (with staff redactions for PII and Exemption 5), and the 6(b)(2) notice provides copies of the final package of materials CPSC intends to disclose along with a cover letter explaining withheld information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Firms have multiple opportunities before disclosure to identify staff errors. The Commission also posts FOIA Request Logs (https://www.cpsc.gov/Newsroom/FOIA/FOIA-Request-Logs) so firms can identify FOIA requesters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commission duty to ensure accuracy and correct materially inaccurate information
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission has an ongoing duty under section 6(b)(6) and 6(b)(7) to ensure that any information it discloses is accurate and not misleading, and, for example, must decline to add materially inaccurate reports of harm to SaferProducts.gov, correct materially inaccurate information, or add corrective information as appropriate (15 U.S.C. 2055a(c)(4)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This duty underpins decisions not to require renotification for every subsequent disclosure but obligates the Commission to verify and correct information it uses or releases.
